title: Anchors as Stored Associations
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which shirt makes you feel at your best?
An anchor is a stored association. You associate wearing that shirt with being on top of your game, and when you go out you feel good. Anybody have a shirt like that?
The mechanism: a cue, such as a shirt, a smell or a song, is linked in memory to a feeling, so meeting the cue brings the feeling back.
I asked the group to look around their rooms for positive anchors. You have kinesthetic anchors, smells and tastes, and that your senses lead you to anchors and triggers.
A student said: ninety percent of our lives is a kind of trance state, with a consistent level, and anchors change the level. This is his claim and is to be verified.
I said that I have to control my own emotions because I am vulnerable to them, and that some days I am different from others.
So a person can place cues on purpose, where they want the feeling to come back. That is the step the exercise asks for.
Next idea: setting an anchor for another person. The next lesson, "Setting an anchor for someone else", builds on this definition.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the clothes, place or song that anchors your best.
Write a smell or taste that does it.
Write the range of your mood this week.
Write the anchor you want more of.
Write where you will place it.

check.q: A song reliably puts someone in a confident mood before a meeting. In the lesson's terms, what is the song?
choices: A reward given for a meeting that went well in the past
A rule the person made up to help them stay disciplined
A cue linked to a feeling, which is an anchor
A habit that the person repeats without noticing it

check.q: Why does the lesson ask people to look around their rooms?
choices: To remove objects that could distract them while they work
To find positive anchors that are already there
To count how many things in the room belong to the person
To decide which objects they would like to buy next

check.q: How should the claim about daily life being mostly a trance state be treated?
choices: As a student's claim that is still to be verified
As a fact the lesson has already proved
As a rule every person in the group must accept
As a claim that proves anchors never change a mood

recap: An anchor is a stored association: a cue linked to a feeling. Your senses lead you to anchors; place the ones you want on purpose.
